# NCLEX-RN Todo List

## **3-6 Months Before Exam**
- [ ] Register for NCLEX through your state's Board of Nursing
- [ ] Receive Authorization to Test (ATT) and schedule exam date
- [ ] Choose a review course (UWorld, Kaplan, Hurst, ATI, etc.)
- [ ] Create a realistic study schedule (6-8 weeks minimum)
- [ ] Gather study materials and resources

## **Study Phase (6-8 Weeks)**
- [ ] Review content by body systems
- [ ] Complete 75-100 practice questions DAILY
- [ ] Focus on weak content areas identified through practice tests
- [ ] Review lab values and normal ranges
- [ ] Study prioritization and delegation concepts
- [ ] Master SATA (Select All That Apply) questions
- [ ] Review pharmacology (top 200-300 drugs)
- [ ] Understand nursing processes and critical thinking
- [ ] Practice test-taking strategies
- [ ] Take at least 2-3 full-length practice exams

## **2 Weeks Before Exam**
- [ ] Take a comprehensive practice test
- [ ] Review rationales for ALL incorrect answers
- [ ] Create flashcards for weak areas
- [ ] Focus on high-yield topics (safety, infection control, prioritization)
- [ ] Review common NCLEX formulas and calculations

## **1 Week Before Exam**
- [ ] Light review only—avoid cramming
- [ ] Review test-day procedures and rules
- [ ] Visit test center location if possible
- [ ] Prepare identification documents
- [ ] Get adequate sleep (7-8 hours nightly)

## **Day Before Exam**
- [ ] Do light review or rest completely
- [ ] Prepare clothes and snacks for test day
- [ ] Avoid alcohol and heavy foods
- [ ] Go to bed early
- [ ] Set multiple alarms

## **Exam Day**
- [ ] Eat a healthy breakfast
- [ ] Arrive 30 minutes early
- [ ] Bring required ID (2 forms, including 1 photo ID)
- [ ] Stay calm and trust your preparation
- [ ] Read each question carefully
- [ ] Use test-taking strategies
- [ ] Take breaks if needed

## **After the Exam**
- [ ] Avoid discussing exam content
- [ ] Wait for Quick Results (48 hours)
- [ ] Celebrate when you pass! 🎉

**Good luck—you've got this!** 💙
